outcomes: A consumer that stores or reads a screenshots manifest decodes it against the published schema or the Go decoder, not against a copy of the writer's types
The schema, the Go decoder and the fixture corpus accept and refuse the same manifests, except for the rules the schema names as ones it cannot express
A consumer knows the largest manifest and the largest capture file it has to accept
nonGoals: The PNG files: the manifest names and hashes them, and a reader checks the bytes it holds against sha256
How pages are selected, served and captured, which putnami change screenshots owns
Storing or showing the screenshots on a hosted change page
A TypeScript decoder: no TypeScript code reads the manifest

text: The manifest is the file screenshots.json; its protocolVersion is 1 and its schema is published at https://putnami.dev/schemas/putnami-screenshots-v1.json.

The schema carries that $id and pins that version. Its members match the Go types, and its closed sets match the Go sets: the sides before and after, the viewports desktop (1440x900 at scale 1) and mobile (390x844 at scale 2), the schemes light and dark.
A manifest fails as a whole, with stable codes, on an unknown, a duplicate or a missing member, and on trailing data.

It fails on another protocolVersion, on a project that is no normalized workspace-relative directory, and on a baseSHA or a headSHA that is no full lowercase commit sha of 40 or 64 hexadecimal characters.
A page fails on a file that is no normalized relative path, on a route or a path that does not start with a slash, on a page that neither side holds, and on a route listed twice.
A capture fails on a file that is no .png name without a directory, on a file listed twice, and on a side, a viewport or a scheme outside its closed set.
It fails on a sha256 that is not 64 lowercase hexadecimal characters, on a status that is no HTTP status from 100 to 599, and on a url that is no absolute http or https URL.
A manifest holds exactly one capture per route, side, viewport and scheme, for each side that holds the page: four captures for a page one side holds, eight for a page both hold.
A capture whose route is none of the pages, or whose side does not hold its page, is refused, and so is a missing or a repeated capture.
Every valid fixture validates, every invalid fixture fails with its expected code, every expected code is registered, and every registered code but the three size bounds has a fixture.
The schema accepts every valid fixture and refuses every invalid one, except those whose rule its description names as one a schema cannot express.
A manifest holds at most 512 pages and 4096 captures, and its file is at most 4 MiB. A capture file is at most 64 MiB. A text member is at most 2048 bytes, and a capture file name at most 255.
The decoder refuses a manifest past a bound, and Marshal refuses to write one.
Marshal validates a manifest before it serializes it, so a writer that goes through the protocol cannot write a manifest the decoder refuses.
A marshaled manifest is indented JSON with one trailing newline that parses back to the same value.
